title: Annotatio III §.X (4) close: Thyestean charges hit Gnostics only; ancients lack Adoration/Elevations/Circumgestations; stop before (5)
pass_a_gloss: That the Thyestean Banquets of which Christians were sometimes accused pertained to the Gnostics alone (numbered with Christians only by most open malice), but by true Christians — without any mention of the Sacred Eucharist injected, much less the least exposition or defense of this Mystery undertaken — were held and exploded as mere calumny, is better known than need be said more lengthily here. Nay the constant and perpetual defect among the ancient Christians of the Praxis and Rites indissolubly annexed to Transsubstantiation (such as Adoration, Elevation, Circumgestation of the Sacrament), invented in more recent centuries, is to be judged to testify amply enough that Transsubstantiation was utterly unknown to them.
pass_b_english: Thyestean banquet charges stuck to Gnostics alone (maliciously counted as Christians); true Christians never even mentioned the Eucharist there, much less explained or defended this mystery — mere calumny, exploded.
And the ancients’ constant lack of later Transsubstantiation-rites (Adoration, Elevation, Circumgestation) amply shows they utterly ignored Transsubstantiation.
source_text: Thyesteas Coenas, quarum quandoque Christiani arguebantur, ad Gnosticos solos (non nisi per apertissimam malitiam Christianis annumeratos) pertinuisse, à veris autem Christianis, citra omnem Eucharistiæ S. mentionem injectam, nedum Mysterii hujus expositionem defensionemque susceptam vel minimam, pro mera calumnia habitas explosasque fuisse, notius est, quàm ut hoc loco prolixius dici debeat. Quin Praxios Rituumque, Transsubstantiationi indissolubiliter annexorum (quales sunt Sacramenti Adoratio, Elevatio, Circumgestatio) recentioribus seculis adinventæ, apud veteres Christianos constans atque perpetuus defectus, de Transsubstantiatione ab his penitus ignorata prolixè satis testari censendus est.
